- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk aversion or market correction.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5% of prior peak or adjust downward only if sentiment remains negative.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ true values if sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or bearish), model often underperforms; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to account for hidden downside risk.
